entries.reference_used: 这次评审我先把背景交代一下。上半年我们把语音笔记的转写链路整个重写了一遍，主要解决三个问题：一是长录音的内存占用过高，二是中英混合场景下的断句不稳定，三是任务提取会把别人的事情算到用户头上。重写之后，转写的峰值内存下降了大约四成，断句错误明显减少，任务归属也加了一道复核。下半年的重点会转到检索这一侧，我们打算把关键词检索和向量检索合并成一路混合召回，再用倒数排名融合来排序。这块的难点不在算法本身，而在于本地设备的算力有限，嵌入模型必须足够小，同时又不能牺牲中文的召回质量。另外还有一个容易被忽略的问题，就是用户的笔记数量增长以后，全库检索的延迟会明显上升，所以我们需要提前设计增量索引和缓存策略。以上是背景，接下来说具体方案。

entries.transcript:
Let me set the context before we go into the details.
In the first half of the year,
we rewrote the entire transcription pipeline
for voice notes, mainly to solve three problems,
memory pressure on long recordings,
unstable sentence segmentation
when Chinese and English are mixed in one utterance,
and task extraction that assigned
other people's action items to the user.
After the rewrite peak memory
during transcription dropped by roughly 40%,
segmentation errors became far less frequent,
and task ownership now goes through a second review pass.
For the second half of the year,
we will shift our attention to retrieval.
The plan is to merge keyword search and vector search
into a single hybrid recall path,
and then order the results with reciprocal rank fusion.
The hard part is not the algorithm itself,
but the limited compute budget on a local device.
The embedding model has to stay small
without sacrificing recall quality in Chinese.
There is also a problem that is easy to overlook,
which is that latency for a full library search
grows noticeably once a user accumulates thousands of notes,
So we need incremental indexing
and a caching strategy well before that point.
entries.reference_used: Let me set the context before we go into the details. In the first half of the year we rewrote the entire transcription pipeline for voice notes, mainly to solve three problems: memory pressure on long recordings, unstable sentence segmentation when Chinese and English are mixed in one utterance, and task extraction that assigned other people's action items to the user. After the rewrite, peak memory during transcription dropped by roughly forty percent, segmentation errors became far less frequent, and task ownership now goes through a second review pass. For the second half of the year we will shift our attention to retrieval. The plan is to merge keyword search and vector search into a single hybrid recall path, and then order the results with reciprocal rank fusion. The hard part is not the algorithm itself, but the limited compute budget on a local device: the embedding model has to stay small without sacrificing recall quality in Chinese. There is also a problem that is easy to overlook, which is that latency for a full library search grows noticeably once a user accumulates thousands of notes, so we need incremental indexing and a caching strategy well before that point.

entries.transcript:
Let me set the context before we go into the details.
In the first half of the year, we rewrote the entire transcription pipeline for these notes,
mainly to solve three problems, memory pressure on long recordings, unstable sentence segmentation
when Chinese and English are mixed in one utterance, and task extraction data sign
data people's action items to the user. After the rewrite, peak memory during transcription dropped
by roughly 40 percent, segmentation errors became far less frequent, and task ownership now goes
through a secondary U-pass. For the second half of the year, we will shift our attention to retrial.
The plan is to merge keyword search and actor search into a single hybrid recall path,
and then order the results with reciprocal rank fusion. The hard part is not the algorithm itself,
but the limited compute budget on local SDE and BDD-NG model has to stay small without sacrificing
recall quality in Chinese. There is also a problem that is easy to overlook,
which is that latency for full library search grows noticeably once a user accumulates thousands
of notes, so we need incremental indexing and CSC-CHANG strategy well before that point.
entries.reference_used: Let me set the context before we go into the details. In the first half of the year we rewrote the entire transcription pipeline for voice notes, mainly to solve three problems: memory pressure on long recordings, unstable sentence segmentation when Chinese and English are mixed in one utterance, and task extraction that assigned other people's action items to the user. After the rewrite, peak memory during transcription dropped by roughly forty percent, segmentation errors became far less frequent, and task ownership now goes through a second review pass. For the second half of the year we will shift our attention to retrieval. The plan is to merge keyword search and vector search into a single hybrid recall path, and then order the results with reciprocal rank fusion. The hard part is not the algorithm itself, but the limited compute budget on a local device: the embedding model has to stay small without sacrificing recall quality in Chinese. There is also a problem that is easy to overlook, which is that latency for a full library search grows noticeably once a user accumulates thousands of notes, so we need incremental indexing and a caching strategy well before that point.
